cpu_spike.title: CPU Spike on Payment Service
cpu_spike.description: payment-service CPU is spiking due to a runaway regex validation in the new payment verification module deployed 20 minutes ago.

logs: [ERROR] PaymentVerification: regex timeout after 30000ms on input validation
[ERROR] RequestHandler: thread pool exhausted — 0/50 threads available
[WARN] HealthCheck: response time 4200ms exceeds 1000ms threshold
[ERROR] PaymentVerification: regex timeout after 30000ms on input validation
[ERROR] CircuitBreaker: OPEN state — payment-verification endpoint
[FATAL] PaymentService: OOM risk — heap usage at 89% after GC
[ERROR] Kubernetes: Liveness probe failed 3 consecutive times
[WARN] LoadBalancer: removing payment-service-pod-3 from rotation
[WARN] Upstream payment-service: 504 Gateway Timeout
[ERROR] CircuitBreaker: payment-service circuit OPEN
[WARN] Retry storm detected: 3x normal retry rate to payment-service

memory_leak.title: Memory Leak in Order Service
memory_leak.description: order-service is leaking memory due to unclosed database cursors in the batch order export feature. OOM kill estimated in 30 minutes.

logs: [WARN] MemoryMonitor: heap usage 72% and climbing (baseline: 45%)
[WARN] GarbageCollector: full GC taking 1200ms (baseline: 50ms)
[ERROR] DatabasePool: cursor leak detected — 847 open cursors (limit: 1000)
[WARN] MemoryMonitor: heap usage 81% — OOM kill threshold at 95%
[ERROR] BatchExport: cursor not closed in export_orders_to_csv()
[WARN] GarbageCollector: full GC taking 3400ms — stop-the-world pause
[ERROR] MemoryMonitor: heap usage 89% — ETA to OOM: ~12 minutes
[FATAL] Kubernetes: pod order-service-pod-2 OOMKilled (exit code 137)

cascading_failure.title: Cascading Failure from Database Latency
cascading_failure.description: postgres-primary is experiencing a long-running analytical query that is locking tables. This causes connection pool exhaustion in upstream services, leading to a full cascade of 5xx errors.

logs: [WARN] SlowQuery: query running for 180s — SELECT * FROM orders JOIN inventory... (analytics dashboard)
[ERROR] ConnectionPool: max connections reached (300/300)
[WARN] LockManager: table 'orders' lock held for 120s by PID 4821
[ERROR] ConnectionPool: 47 queries waiting in queue (max queue: 50)
[FATAL] PostgreSQL: too many connections for role 'app_user'
[ERROR] DatabasePool: connection acquisition timeout after 30s
[ERROR] PaymentProcessor: failed to record transaction — DB unavailable
[ERROR] CircuitBreaker: postgres-primary circuit OPEN after 5 failures
[WARN] Fallback: returning cached payment status (stale: 5 min)
[ERROR] DatabasePool: connection timeout — all connections busy
[ERROR] OrderProcessor: cannot create order — DB write failed
[WARN] RetryPolicy: exhausted 3 retries for order creation
[ERROR] API: returning 503 Service Unavailable to client
[ERROR] Upstream: payment-service returned 503
[ERROR] Upstream: order-service returned 503
[WARN] ErrorRate: 42% of requests failing (threshold: 5%)
[ERROR] AlertManager: CRITICAL alert triggered — cascading failure detected

bad_deployment.title: Bad Canary Deployment on Inventory Service
bad_deployment.description: A canary deployment of inventory-service v2.4.0 introduced a breaking API change. The new version returns inventory counts as strings instead of integers, causing JSON parse errors in order-service.

logs: [INFO] Deployment: canary rollout inventory-service v2.4.0 (25% traffic)
[INFO] Deployment: image updated from v2.3.1 to v2.4.0
[WARN] API: response schema changed — 'quantity' field type: int -> string
[INFO] HealthCheck: inventory-service v2.4.0 pods healthy
[ERROR] InventoryClient: JSON parse error — expected int for 'quantity', got string '150'
[ERROR] OrderValidator: cannot validate order — inventory check failed
[ERROR] InventoryClient: JSON parse error — expected int for 'quantity', got string '0'
[WARN] ErrorRate: 12% of orders failing (affects 25% of traffic via canary)
[ERROR] InventoryClient: type mismatch in deserialize_inventory_response()
[WARN] AlertManager: error rate threshold exceeded on order-service
